flashcard_questions.q: What does the word atonement literally mean?
flashcard_questions.a: “At-one-ment” — making God and humanity at one again.

flashcard_questions.q: What is concupiscence in Catholic teaching?
flashcard_questions.a: The tendency to sin that remains even after baptism.

flashcard_questions.q: How do Catholics believe original sin is removed?
flashcard_questions.a: Through the sacrament of baptism, which is why babies are baptised.

flashcard_questions.q: What do liberal Christians say about the story of Adam and Eve?
flashcard_questions.a: That it is a myth teaching a truth, not a literal historical event.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse teaches that everyone has sinned and falls short of God’s glory?
Which verse do Catholics use to argue that faith needs action?
flashcard_questions.a: James 2:17 — “Faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead.”

flashcard_questions.q: What do Reformed Protestants believe about how salvation is received?
flashcard_questions.a: By grace alone through faith alone, never by earning it through good deeds.

flashcard_questions.q: What do Catholics believe is needed for salvation besides faith?
flashcard_questions.a: Good works, which grace enables and which also contribute to salvation.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Jesus promise the Holy Spirit would do, in John 14:26?
flashcard_questions.a: Teach believers all things, as the Advocate sent by the Father.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Christians particularly emphasise the gifts of the Holy Spirit?
What does substitutionary atonement claim about Jesus’s death?
flashcard_questions.a: Jesus took the place of sinners and bore the punishment they deserved.

flashcard_questions.q: Who is the satisfaction theory of atonement associated with?
What does the moral example view say about Jesus’s death?
flashcard_questions.a: It was a supreme example of self-sacrificing love that inspires Christians.

flashcard_questions.q: Which prophecy do Christians believe Jesus fulfilled on the cross?
flashcard_questions.a: Isaiah 53:5 — “by his wounds we are healed.”

notes: 14 cards: 4 denomination→position (Catholic baptism, liberal view, Reformed grace alone, Catholic works), 4 belief→source (Romans 3:23, James 2:17, John 14:26, Isaiah 53:5), 3 argument→view (substitutionary, satisfaction, moral example), 2 term→definition (atonement, concupiscence), 1 attribution (Anselm).
